_comment: Curated, evidence-backed title-convention overrides used ONLY as a last resort by classifyTenureTrackWithEvidence, after every explicit tenure/non-tenure phrase check (stored field, title, description) has come up empty. Each rule fires only for one specific institution's own documented title naming convention -- never a blanket 'this college defaults to X' guess. Add a rule only with a citable, authoritative source (the institution's own faculty affairs / academic tracks page), and keep titlePattern as narrow as the source's own language, so a plain/ambiguous title at that institution still correctly falls through to unclassified rather than being guessed.

rules.college: Columbia University in the City of New York
rules.note: CUIMC's non-tenure track is the 'at CUMC' track: titles in this track carry the academic rank plus the suffix 'at CUMC' (e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Medicine at CUMC'). The unmodified/plain title without that suffix is the Tenure Track, but CUIMC's own docs do not confirm the reverse (plain title => always tenure-track), so this rule is intentionally one-directional and does not attempt to classify plain titles.

Miller School of Medicine's Clinical Educator (non-tenure) track uses 'Professor of Clinical [Department]' / 'Clinical [rank] Professor' titles (e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Clinical - Anesthesiology'), distinct from the Tenure track's unmodified titles. This is also a standard cross-institutional academic-medicine naming convention (Yale, NYU, and others use the same 'Clinical Professor' / 'Professor of Clinical X' pattern for their non-tenure clinician-educator titles), but scoped to this institution only since 'clinical' in a title is not a safe global signal -- some institutions use it loosely for unpaid/volunteer clinical faculty or for tenure-track physician-scientists.

rules.college: The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston
rules.note: UTMB's own IHOP faculty-titles policy: 'Non-tenure tracks will have a mission designation following the rank: research, instruction, or clinical practice (i.e. Assistant Professor of Clinical Practice).' Matches a rank word (Professor/Professors/Instructor) followed within a short span by one of those three mission designations (also covers the 'Clinic Practice' typo variant seen in the live data), plus the literal 'N-T Trk' (Non-Tenure Track) abbreviation UTMB uses directly in some titles. A plain rank + department title with no mission designation (e.g. 'Assistant Professor, Cardiovascular Medicine') is NOT matched -- UTMB postings don't always state the mission designation, so those correctly stay unclassified rather than being guessed.

SMD Faculty Regulations (PDF) define three distinct non-tenure title series, each confirmed by exact quoted policy language: (1) '[Rank] OF CLINICAL (DEPARTMENT)' e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Clinical Medicine' -- for faculty whose contributions are 'principally clinical or other professional services', explicitly 'not considered academic in the same sense' as the tenure-eligible track; (2) 'CLINICAL [Rank]' prefix e.g. 'Clinical Assistant Professor' -- the Voluntary Clinical Faculty series for unpaid community-based appointments; (3) 'RESEARCH [Rank]' prefix e.g. 'Research Assistant Professor' -- soft-money appointments that 'terminate concurrently with the cessation of the program, grant, or contract.' Deliberately does NOT match a plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Instructor'/'Faculty' title: the regulations state the academic titles for the main (potentially tenure-track) series 'are the same, regardless of the components of professional activity' (Research/Scholarship/Clinical), so a plain title genuinely cannot be resolved from title text alone and correctly stays unclassified.

rules.collegePattern: ^(?:Binghamton University|SUNY Buffalo State University|SUNY Canton|SUNY Cobleskill|SUNY College at Potsdam|SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry|SUNY College of Optometry|SUNY Cortland|SUNY Delhi|SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University|SUNY Maritime College|SUNY Morrisville|SUNY Old Westbury|SUNY Oneonta|SUNY Oswego|SUNY Plattsburgh|SUNY Polytechnic Institute|SUNY Upstate Medical University|SUNY at Fredonia|State University of New York at New Paltz|Stony Brook University|University at Albany|University at Buffalo)$
rules.note: System-wide SUNY HR policy (suny.edu, 'Qualified Academic Rank Titles'): 'Qualified academic ranks are not "tenure track"... By definition, Qualified Academic Rank is: Rank held by those members of the academic staff having titles of lecturer, or titles of academic rank preceded by the designations "clinical" or "visiting" or other similar designations.' ('visiting' is already handled globally by CLEARLY_NON_TENURE_TITLE_RE, so only 'clinical [rank]' and bare 'lecturer' are added here.) Scoped by collegePattern to SUNY's state-operated campuses (university centers, health science centers, and colleges of technology/arts & sciences) that follow this UUP/SUNY-system HR title schema -- deliberately excludes SUNY's separately-governed community colleges (e.g. SUNY Broome, SUNY Onondaga, SUNY Orange, SUNY Westchester, SUNY Jefferson, SUNY Ulster, SUNY Ncc), which have distinct local-sponsor governance and are not confirmed to use the same title schema. The 'clinical' branch allows a wider span after the word so it also matches multi-rank slash chains used heavily at Stony Brook/Buffalo/Downstate postings (e.g. 'Clinical Assistant/Associate/Full Professor') -- an earlier, narrower version that only allowed one optional assistant/associate word missed these entirely.

UK's Office for Faculty Advancement lists its faculty title series and confirms tenure status per series: the Regular/Extension/Special/Librarian series are tenure-eligible, while the Research Title Series (AR 2:5), Clinical Title Series (AR 2:6), and Lecturer Series (AR 2:9) are all explicitly non-tenure-track. Matches the 'Clinical [rank]' and 'Research [rank]' prefix conventions, bare '(Senior) Lecturer', and the literal 'Clinical Title Series' phrase seen directly in one live posting title. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant, Associate or Professor in/of [Specialty]' title with no series qualifier -- UK posts the large majority of its faculty jobs this way without stating which title series applies, so those correctly stay unclassified rather than being guessed (only 16 of 88 unclassified UK jobs carry an explicit series qualifier).

OSU's faculty appointments policy (trustees.osu.edu bylaws 3335-7) defines three non-tenure 'fixed term contract appointments that do not entail tenure': the Clinical series ('Clinical instructor, assistant clinical professor, associate clinical professor, or clinical professor'), the Teaching series (same pattern), and the Professional practice series (same pattern) -- matching the 'Assistant Professor - Practice' shorthand seen in live posting titles. Separately, OSU's College of Medicine faculty-tracks page defines 'Associated Faculty' as a non-tenure category explicitly including 'Lecturer and Senior Lecturer'. Deliberately does NOT match OSU's very common 'Physician - ... (Open Rank/Track Faculty)' posting pattern (56 of 83 unclassified OSU jobs): 'Open Rank/Track' is OSU's own phrasing that the appointment track is literally undetermined at posting time (could land on tenure-track, Clinical, or Research faculty depending on the candidate) -- genuinely unresolvable from the title, so it correctly stays unclassified rather than being guessed.

rules.college: The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio
rules.note: UTHSA's IHOP policy (3.1.1 Academic Titles) states only the plain 'Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor' titles are 'Tenure Titles' -- distinct from the '/Clinical' and '/Research' suffixed titles (see the companion false-valued rule below). Two live postings append an explicit ', Tenure' or 'with Tenure' to the plain title to signal this (e.g. 'Chair and Professor, Tenure'), a positive signal not covered by the shared global TENURE_RE pattern (which requires 'position/appointment/rank/role' to precede 'with tenure', not follow it).

rules.college: The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio
rules.note: UTHSA's IHOP policy (3.1.1 Academic Titles), quoted directly: 'Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor are the only academic titles in which faculty members may hold tenure or be on the tenure track.' Non-Tenure Titles are explicitly enumerated: 'Professor/Clinical ... or Professor/Research ...', 'Associate Professor/Clinical ... or Associate Professor/Research ...', 'Assistant Professor/Clinical ... or Assistant Professor/Research ...', 'Instructor/Clinical ... or Instructor/Research ...' (Section A.2.b) -- matching the '[Rank]/Clinical' and '[Rank]/Research' suffix convention seen throughout live posting titles. Section B separately lists 'Other Non-Tenure Titles' including the prefix form ('Clinical Professor, Clinical Associate Professor, Clinical Assistant Professor, Clinical Instructor...'), 'Lecturer'/'Senior Lecturer'/'Distinguished Senior Lecturer', and bare 'Instructor' ('This title denotes a probationary appointment...'). Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Associate Professor'/'Professor' with no suffix, nor the very common 'Open Rank Faculty ...' postings -- both are the Tenure Titles category or genuinely undetermined, and stay correctly unclassified.

SRJC's own live posting text (quoted directly, verified 2026-09-10 on an 'Associate Faculty - Chemistry' posting): 'Santa Rosa Junior College is currently accepting applications on a continuous basis to establish a pool for associate faculty assignments. Associate assignments may be temporary, part-time and/or on-call... A part-time faculty assignment may not exceed a total of 67% of an annual full-time assignment.' All 70 of SRJC's unclassified postings at the time used the exact title prefix 'Associate Faculty - [Subject]'. Scoped to this one college (not generalized to 'Associate Faculty' at other California community colleges) since only this institution's own posting language was directly verified.

CWU's Faculty Code structurally separates 'academic rank' (professor/associate professor/assistant professor -- the tenure-eligible titles) from 'professional designation' (clinical faculty, senior research associate, research associate, senior lecturer, lecturer, visiting professor, coach) as two distinct faculty categories (Section I.A.1.a). Corroborated by the CWU/United Faculty of Central CBA, which describes Lecturer positions as a non-tenure track faculty category. Matches the dominant 'Lecturer Pool - [Subject]' posting pattern (55 of 65 unclassified CWU jobs) plus the literal 'Nonpermanent' qualifier seen on one posting.

UW's Academic Personnel & Faculty site (ap.washington.edu) documents five professorial tracks: Tenure, 'Without Tenure by reason of funding (WOT)', Research, Teaching, and Clinical Practice -- with 'Tenure status: N/A' listed explicitly for every rank in the last four. WOT specifically means faculty whose salary comes from grants/contracts/clinical revenue rather than state-appropriated funds, so they don't hold tenure even though fully integrated into department activities. Separately, UW's 'Acting Titles' policy page confirms: 'acting faculty appointments do not have implications for the award of tenure or for promotion in a clock-managed rank' (used for ABD candidates and postdocs past the terminal-degree limit, pending conversion to a regular title once the degree is conferred). Matches the '(WOT)' abbreviation, 'of Clinical Practice' suffix, 'Clinical [rank]'/'Clinical Faculty' prefix, 'Teaching/Research [rank]' prefix in either word order, and 'Acting [rank]' prefix. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor' with no qualifier, nor administrative/dean titles -- both stay correctly unclassified.

USF's Provost office confirms the 'Professor of Instruction Series' (Assistant/Associate/Professor of Instruction) is explicitly for 'full-time, non-tenure track teaching positions', alongside a separate non-tenure 'Instructor Series' (Assistant/Associate/Senior Instructor) -- both referred to collectively as 'instructional faculty'. Matches the 'of Instruction' suffix, 'Instructional Faculty' label, and the 'Instructor I'/'Instructor 1' grade notation seen on several clinical/allied-health (APRN, PA) postings. Also matches the explicit 'Clinical Faculty Position' label used on medical-school postings, consistent with the non-tenure clinical-track convention already verified at every other academic medical center in this table (Miami, UTMB, Rochester, UTHSA, UW), though not independently re-confirmed in USF's own documentation. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Open Rank Faculty' posting with no qualifier (26 of 39 unclassified USF jobs) -- correctly stays unclassified.

Weaker evidentiary basis than the other rules in this table -- no explicit written tenure policy was located (search results repeatedly conflated TSTC with the unrelated Texas State University). This rule instead rests on a structural finding, empirically checked against every TSTC posting ever scraped (40 jobs, 28 unique titles): zero contain 'Professor' in any form -- 'Instructor' is the entire title vocabulary. Combined with TSTC's own institutional identity as a state technical/vocational college (welding, HVAC, diesel, electrical lineworker, aviation maintenance, etc., not a research university), 'Instructor' here reads as the sole, terminal job title for this employer rather than an entry pre-tenure rank on an academic ladder. Revisit if a professorial title is ever observed at this college.

UW-Madison's School of Medicine and Public Health (SMPH) defines six faculty tracks: Clinical Health Sciences (CHS), Clinician Teacher (CT), Tenured/Tenure-Track, Research Professor, Teaching Professor, and Clinical Adjunct. Quoted directly: 'UW-Madison only recognizes the tenure track faculty as full faculty members of the university. The other categories of SMPH faculty are considered academic staff according to UW-Madison policies.' Matches the '(CHS)'/'(CT)' abbreviations seen throughout live posting titles (including bare, un-parenthesized forms like 'Professor CHS-Cornea Service'), plus 'Research Professor', 'Teaching Professor'/'Teaching Faculty', and the 'Clinical [rank]' prefix convention. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor' with no track qualifier (9 of 35 unclassified UW-Madison jobs, including several outside the medical school entirely, e.g. Political Science) -- correctly stays unclassified.

UVM Larner College of Medicine's Faculty Handbook defines one Tenure Pathway and four Non-Tenure, Ranked pathways (Clinical, Clinical Scholar, Education Scholar, Research Scholar) plus a Non-Salaried Volunteer pathway -- quoted directly, the four ranked non-tenure pathways 'are all salaried, promotable positions that do not lead to appointment with tenure.' The Clinical Pathway uses a distinct title prefix ('Clinical Instructor, Clinical Assistant Professor, Clinical Associate Professor, and Clinical Professor'). Critically, the Clinical Scholar Pathway's titles are the SAME plain 'Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, and Professor' as the Tenure Pathway -- the handbook gives no title-level way to tell them apart, so only postings that explicitly state 'Clinical Scholar Pathway' in the title (as UVM's own postings consistently do) are safely classifiable; a plain title with no pathway named stays correctly unclassified. Also matches 'Clinical Academic [Specialty]' and 'Clinical Radiologist' department-level labels seen on live Radiology postings -- not a named handbook pathway verbatim, but consistent with the 'Clinical' qualifier being this institution's one defining non-tenure signal everywhere else.

rules.collegePattern: ^(?:Alamance Community College|Asheville-Buncombe Technical Community College|Beaufort County Community College|Bladen Community College|Blue Ridge Community College \(NC\)|Brunswick Community College|Caldwell Community College and Technical Institute|Cape Fear Community College|Carteret Community College|Catawba Valley Community College|Central Carolina Community College|Central Piedmont Community College|Cleveland Community College|Coastal Carolina Community College|College of the Albemarle|Craven Community College|Davidson-Davie Community College|Durham Technical Community College|Edgecombe Community College|Fayetteville Technical Community College|Forsyth Technical Community College|Gaston College|Guilford Technical Community College|Halifax Community College|Haywood Community College|Isothermal Community College|James Sprunt Community College|Johnston Community College|Lenoir Community College|Martin Community College|Mayland Community College|McDowell Technical Community College|Mitchell Community College|Montgomery Community College|Nash Community College|Pamlico Community College|Piedmont Community College|Pitt Community College|Randolph Community College|Richmond Community College|Roanoke-Chowan Community College|Robeson Community College|Rockingham Community College|Rowan-Cabarrus Community College|Sampson Community College|Sandhills Community College|South Piedmont Community College|Southeastern Community College \(NC\)|Southwestern Community College \(NC\)|Stanly Community College|Surry Community College|Tri-County Community College|Vance-Granville Community College|Wake Technical Community College|Wayne Community College|Western Piedmont Community College|Wilkes Community College|Wilson Community College)$
rules.note: The NC State Board of Community Colleges Code (SBCCC) -- the governing regulatory document for all 58 public NC community colleges -- contains zero mentions of the word 'tenure' or 'career status' anywhere across its full ~540 pages; employment there is instead categorized as 'permanent, probationary, or time-limited appointment' (SBCCC 8C SBCCC 200.94), a distinct construct from academic tenure. Corroborated by NC General Statute Chapter 115D (Community Colleges) and a 2023 state legislative bill explicitly targeting tenure at 'UNC System universities AND community colleges', which only makes sense to mention community colleges preemptively if referring to that same non-tenure 'permanent status', not a pre-existing tenure system. Since no NC community college position can be on a tenure track by institutional design, titlePattern intentionally matches every title (not keyword-scoped) -- 214 of 216 unclassified NC-community-college postings contain 'Instructor' or 'Faculty' anyway, but the remaining two ('Department Chair of Horticulture Technology', 'EMT/EMS/Paramedic ... Instructors' with a missed plural) are equally covered by the underlying institutional fact rather than needing broader keyword patterns. Scoped to control=public only -- excludes Louisburg College, a private 2-year junior college in NC not governed by SBCCC/Chapter 115D.

ECU's Faculty Manual (Part VIII, Section I: Personnel Policies and Procedures for the Faculty of East Carolina University), quoted directly: 'Appointments are made at the academic ranks of assistant professor, associate professor, and professor. These are the only ranks that may involve a permanent tenure commitment. Appointments to all other titles are for a definite term and do not involve a permanent tenure commitment.' The Clinical title series (Clinical Instructor, Clinical Assistant Professor, Clinical Associate Professor, Clinical Professor) is defined separately under the 'Titles of Fixed-Term Appointments' heading -- never under the tenure-eligible rank definitions -- with explicit fixed-term language, e.g. 'Appointment to the title of Clinical Instructor may be made for a fixed term of up to three years.' This is a university-wide section of the Faculty Manual, not limited to one school, and matches both a Dentistry posting ('Advanced Education in General Dentistry Faculty - Clinical Assistant Professor') and a Communication Sciences and Disorders posting seen in the live data. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Associate Professor'/'Professor' title with no Clinical qualifier, which remains a tenure-eligible rank per the same manual section and correctly stays unclassified without further evidence.

Penn State Policy AC21 ('Definition of Academic Ranks') defines a distinct 'Section C: Ranks for Non-Tenure-Line Research Faculty' covering Researcher, Assistant Research Professor, Associate Research Professor, and Research Professor, separate from the tenure-line Assistant/Associate/Professor ranks defined in Section A. Corroborated by Penn State's College of Earth and Mineral Sciences AC21 supplement, quoted directly: 'Research ranks and instructional ranks are intended for individuals who are engaged primarily in research or teaching respectively and are always Non-Tenure-Line in nature,' and by the Eberly College of Science (the college housing astrophysics, matching a live 'Assistant Research Professor - Time Domain and Multi-Messenger Astrophysics' posting) listing 'research professor'/'associate research professor' promotions explicitly as non-tenure-line faculty promotions. AC21 is a university-wide policy, so collegePattern covers 'The Pennsylvania State University' and every Penn State commonwealth-campus college string (e.g. 'Pennsylvania State University-Penn State Harrisburg') seen in the live data. Matches both title-word orderings ('Research Assistant Professor' and 'Assistant Research Professor') plus bare 'Research Professor' and 'Researcher'. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Associate Professor'/'Professor' title with no Research qualifier, which remains tenure-line and correctly stays unclassified without further evidence.

Ivy Tech's own IPEDS Human Resources Survey submission (2024-25 collection, UnitID 150987) answers 'No' to the federal survey question 'Does your institution have a tenure system?' -- all 1,120 full-time instructional staff reported for Fall 2024 fall exclusively under IPEDS categories pre-labeled 'Not on Tenure Track' (Annual Contract: 1,114; Less-than-Annual Contract: 6), with zero staff in any Multi-Year-Contract or Indefinite-duration tenure/tenure-track column across every rank. This is Ivy Tech's own authoritative self-report to the federal government (submitted under a data-quality certification), the same evidentiary standing as reading a governing state code directly. Ivy Tech is statutorily one of Indiana's seven 'state educational institutions' under IC 21-7-13-32, so the state's general tenure statute (IC 21-39.5) could in principle apply, but Ivy Tech's own federal filing confirms no tenure system exists there in practice. Since no Ivy Tech position can be on a tenure track by institutional design, titlePattern intentionally matches every title (same approach as the NC community-college rule) -- live postings like 'Full-Time Faculty - Nursing' and 'CNA/QMA Faculty' carry no rank or track qualifier because none exists at this institution.

rules.collegePattern: ^(?:Arapahoe Community College|Colorado Northwestern Community College|Community College of Aurora|Community College of Denver|Front Range Community College|Lamar Community College|Morgan Community College|Northeastern Junior College|Otero College|Otero Junior College|Pikes Peak State College|Pikes Peak Community College|Pueblo Community College|Red Rocks Community College|Trinidad State College|Trinidad State Junior College)$
rules.note: The Colorado Community College System's (CCCS) own system-wide Board Policies and System President's Procedures -- which govern faculty employment at all 13 CCCS colleges, including individual colleges' own HR pages, which point back to these same system-wide policy numbers rather than defining separate local tenure systems -- never use the word 'tenure' to describe faculty status. Instead CCCS uses a contract-based framework: BP 3-10 ('Administration of Personnel'), quoted directly: 'Regular Faculty: contracted on a provisional or non-provisional basis...' and 'Limited Faculty: hold contracts that are expressly limited so as to carry no expectancy of continued employment beyond the term of the contract.' SP 3-20c ('Issuance and Termination of Faculty Contracts') and BP 3-20 ('Due Process for Faculty') likewise describe only a provisional-to-non-provisional contract progression and a 'Non-Renewal' concept, with no tenure vocabulary anywhere. Unlike the NC precedent, CCCS policy does not contain an explicit denial sentence ('faculty are not eligible for tenure') -- it simply never introduces the concept, building an entirely separate contract vocabulary instead; the underlying Colorado statute (CRS Title 23, Article 60) could not be directly read to independently confirm this at the state-law level, so this rule rests on the CCCS board-policy layer alone, which is nonetheless CCCS's own authoritative, board-adopted governing document controlling faculty employment terms system-wide. Since no covered college's faculty can be on a tenure track by institutional design, titlePattern intentionally matches every title (same approach as the NC rule).

rules.collegePattern: ^(?:Aiken Technical College|Central Carolina Technical College|Denmark Technical College|Florence-Darlington Technical College|Greenville Technical College|Horry-Georgetown Technical College|Midlands Technical College|Northeastern Technical College|Orangeburg[\s-]Calhoun Technical College|Piedmont Technical College|Spartanburg Community College|Technical College of the Lowcountry|Tri-County Technical College|Trident Technical College|Williamsburg Technical College|York Technical College)$
rules.note: South Carolina's 16 technical colleges are governed by the SC State Board for Technical and Comprehensive Education (SBTCE) under S.C. Code Title 59, Chapter 53. Section 59-53-20, quoted directly: 'All personnel employed in the institutions and programs within the jurisdiction and control of [SBTCE] are designated state employees ... and are subject to ... the state personnel system.' The word 'tenure' does not appear anywhere in Chapter 53. The SC Department of Administration's State Human Resources Regulations (which Sec. 59-53-20 subjects technical-college employees to) define career security instead as civil-service 'Permanent'/'Covered' status reached after a probationary period -- quoted directly: 'PROBATIONARY EMPLOYEE ... a working test period ... of not more than 2 full academic years' duration for faculty at State technical colleges,' and technical colleges are affirmatively carved OUT of the general 'Instructional Personnel' academic-year definition used for other SC educational agencies. SBTCE Procedure 8-7-100.1 ('Employment Practices') corroborates, defining only three position categories (FTE, temporary, temporary grant/time-limited) with no tenure or continuing-contract category, and states the policy itself 'does not create an employment contract.' Since no covered college's faculty can be on a tenure track by institutional design, titlePattern intentionally matches every title (same approach as the NC rule).

rules.collegePattern: ^(?:Baton Rouge Community College|Bossier Parish Community College|Central Louisiana Technical Community College|Delgado Community College|Fletcher Technical Community College|Louisiana Delta Community College|Northshore Technical Community College|Northwest Louisiana Technical Community College|Nunez Community College|River Parishes Community College|South Louisiana Community College|SOWELA Technical Community College)$
rules.note: The Louisiana Community and Technical College System's (LCTCS) own operative tenure policy, Board Policy #6.021 ('Tenure Rights/Removal'), quoted directly, restricts tenure to a small, closed, legacy population: it applies 'only ... to employees of the LCTCS who were engaged in the performance of the postsecondary vocational-technical school functions of [BESE] and [the Department of Education], prior to July 1, 1999, and who acquired tenure status, prior to July 1, 1999' -- i.e. tenure is not available to any current or new hire, only grandfathered pre-1999 transferees. LCTCS's operative rank/promotion policy for current faculty, Board Policy #1.044 ('Rank, Promotion, Duties, and Responsibilities of Faculty and Staff'), defines the current Instructor/Assistant/Associate/Professor rank system purely in terms of contracts or letters of appointment, with no tenure-track process, criteria, or committee described. Corroborated by Baton Rouge Community College's own Faculty Handbook, in which 'tenure' appears exactly once (quoting an AAUP document title) and rank placement is instead based on years of teaching experience. Note: Policy #1.044 contains one boilerplate cross-reference to a general Louisiana Board of Regents tenure-eligibility rule that appears carried over from a system-wide BoR template used across all Louisiana public postsecondary systems -- it describes no actual LCTCS tenure process and is contradicted by LCTCS's own operative tenure policy (6.021) closing tenure to the pre-1999 legacy group, but is flagged here for transparency. Since no covered college's current faculty can be on a tenure track by institutional design, titlePattern intentionally matches every title (same approach as the NC rule).

MSU's Faculty Handbook (Section V.B, 'Academic Rank') states: 'Faculty tracks at Mississippi State University include tenure-track positions and professional-track positions.' Tenure-Track Positions lists only Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, and Professor (unmodified). Professional-Track Positions includes 'Clinical/Extension/Research Professor Ranks,' immediately followed by the footnote: 'Some Extension and Research positions are tenure-track. Faculty holding a tenure-track Extension or Research position should refer to the tenure-track guidance above' -- an exception carved out explicitly for Extension and Research, and pointedly NOT extended to Clinical. Section V.A adds: 'Professional-track faculty members are eligible for promotion, but not tenure.' MSU's own postings commonly enumerate ranks together (e.g. 'Assistant/Associate/Full Clinical Professor'), so titlePattern matches the literal 'clinical professor'/'clinical instructor' substring anywhere in the title rather than anchoring to a fixed word order, trusting the standard academic-posting convention that a single opening enumerates ranks WITHIN one track rather than spanning tenure and non-tenure tracks in one posting. Deliberately does not match bare 'Professor'/'Extension Professor'/'Research Professor' with no 'Clinical' qualifier (which the handbook's own footnote says can be tenure-track), nor cases where 'clinical' modifies an unrelated noun rather than the rank itself (e.g. 'Director of Clinical Education' -- correctly stays unclassified since 'Clinical' here describes a program, not a title/track).

WesternU's University Faculty Handbook draws a categorical line between 'Regular Faculty' (Professor/Associate/Assistant Professor/Instructor, tenure-track or non-tenure-track per contract) and 'Auxiliary Faculty' (Adjunct/Visiting/Research/Clinical-designated titles), stating Auxiliary titles 'confer faculty status' outside the Regular Faculty tenure framework entirely. The College of Dental Medicine's own handbook is explicit: 'Faculty members with auxiliary appointments are not eligible for Tenure Track appointment.' Independently confirmed at 3 of WesternU's 8 colleges: the College of Osteopathic Medicine (COMP) additionally documents a second, REGULAR (non-Auxiliary) non-tenure-track convention using an infix form -- 'Professor of Clinical [Specialty]'/'Associate Professor of Clinical [Specialty]'/'Assistant Professor of Clinical [Specialty]' -- explicitly grouped under the heading 'Clinical Faculty (Non-Tenure-Track)', which matches live postings like 'Assistant Professor of Clinical Sciences'. titlePattern therefore matches both the Auxiliary prefix form ('Clinical Assistant Professor of Optometry') and the COMP infix form ('Professor of Clinical Sciences'). Confirmed for COMP, College of Dental Medicine, and College of Veterinary Medicine; inherited-but-not-independently-verified for Pharmacy, Optometry, Podiatric Medicine, Graduate Nursing, and Health Sciences. Deliberately does not match bare 'Assistant/Associate Professor'/'Instructor' with no Clinical qualifier, which remains a Regular Faculty title potentially on the tenure track.

Pacific's Faculty Handbook (Section 7.1.4, 'Clinical Appointments'), quoted directly: 'The clinical appointment is a non-tenurable appointment. ... A prefix such as "clinical", or suffix such as "of Practice", or other appropriate prefix or suffix, will be designated for these appointments.' Section 7.1.2 confirms only the unmodified ranks (professor, associate professor, assistant professor) are tenure-eligible. The Arthur A. Dugoni School of Dentistry's own handbook independently corroborates non-tenure treatment for clinically-focused appointments ('No faculty member on the teacher-clinician track is eligible for tenure'). Live Pacific postings consistently self-label this explicitly (e.g. 'Associate Clinical Professor or Clinical Professor (Non-Tenure Track)'). titlePattern allows up to 30 characters between 'clinical' and 'professor'/'instructor' to cover slash-enumerated forms like 'Clinical Assistant / Associate Professor' without requiring the exact word order the Handbook's own prefix form uses. Deliberately requires the literal word 'professor' or 'instructor' to appear near 'clinical', so plain '(Pre-)Clinical Faculty' titles with no professorial rank word (several observed in live data, e.g. dentistry 'Evergreen position' postings) correctly stay unclassified rather than being guessed, as does 'Preclinical' (no word-boundary match against 'clinical').

University of Michigan Standard Practice Guide SPG 201.34-1 ('Classification and Appointment of Instructional Faculty'), a university-wide policy (Ann Arbor, Dearborn, and Flint), quoted directly under 'CLINICAL INSTRUCTIONAL FACULTY': 'Clinical instructional appointments ... are without tenure. The following titles may be used for clinical instructional appointments: clinical professor, clinical associate professor, clinical assistant professor, clinical instructor, or clinical lecturer.' Contrasted directly with the SPG's Tenure Track Faculty section ('Appointments are without tenure but are tenure-track' / 'appointments with these titles are with tenure'). Corroborated by the Medical School's Office of Faculty Affairs, which documents a distinct Clinical Track (since 1986) alongside the Tenure Track and Research Track. Live postings also use a 'Clinical Track' qualifier phrase directly (e.g. 'Clinical Track Assistant/Associate Professor of Restorative Dentistry'), so titlePattern matches both the prefix-title forms and the standalone 'Clinical Track' qualifier. A negative lookbehind excludes any posting phrasing the appointment as an explicit choice between tracks (observed live: 'Assistant/Associate Tenure- or Clinical-Track Professor') -- the track for that specific hire is genuinely undetermined at posting time and correctly stays unclassified, the same treatment already given to Ohio State's 'Open Rank/Track' postings elsewhere in this table.

rules.collegePattern: ^(?:UC Berkeley|UC Davis|UC Irvine|UC Merced|UC Riverside|UC San Francisco|UC Santa Barbara|UC Santa Cruz|UCLA|University of California-San Diego)$
rules.note: The University of California's systemwide Academic Personnel Manual (APM), issued by UCOP and identical across every campus, explicitly separates the tenure-eligible 'regular ranks' faculty from several other series. APM 220-4-b (Professor series), quoted directly: 'Persons appointed to titles in the Professor series form the "regular ranks" faculty of the University. This series is distinct from the following series: Acting Professor series, Adjunct Professor series, Health Sciences Clinical Professor series, Professor in Residence series, Visiting Professor series, Professor of Clinical ___ series, Professor of Teaching series.' APM 278 (Health Sciences Clinical Professor / HSCP), section 278-20: 'Neither tenure nor security of employment is acquired by appointment to a title in this series, regardless of percentage of State funding.' APM 275 (Professor of Clinical ___, i.e. 'Clinical X'/'ClinX'), section 275-20: 'Neither tenure nor security of employment is acquired by appointment to a title in this series' -- and 275-17-a specifies time in this series 'does not count toward service as an Assistant Professor in Residence or any title eligible for tenure.' Both APM sections are systemwide (not campus-specific); campus-level pages (e.g. UCSD, UCLA, UC Irvine) implement but do not alter these definitions. Matches both full names ('Health Sciences Clinical Professor', 'Professor of Clinical [specialty]') and the abbreviations UC postings commonly use ('HSCP', 'Clin X', 'ClinX'). Checked every live UC posting containing any of these terms across all 10 campuses present in the dataset -- several postings offer a choice among multiple non-tenure series in one listing (e.g. 'Adjunct, Clinical X, HS Clinical, In Residence Faculty'), which is still safely classifiable since APM 220-4-b confirms Adjunct, Clinical X, HSCP, and In-Residence are ALL outside the tenure-eligible Professor series -- none is a live alternative in the announcement. Deliberately does not match bare 'Professor'/'Assistant Professor'/'Associate Professor' with no HSCP/Clinical X/Health Sciences qualifier, which is the actual tenure-eligible Ladder Rank series, nor any posting mixing a Ladder Rank/tenure-track option with a clinical-series option (none were found in the live data, but would need separate handling if one appears). Also extended to bare 'Lecturer': UC's Academic Personnel Manual (APM-285) explicitly substitutes the term 'security of employment' for 'tenure' in its Lecturer-series policy ('The term "security of employment" shall be substituted for the term "tenure"'), and as of the May 2024 APM revision the former Lecturer-with-Security-of-Employment series was renamed to 'Assistant/Associate/Professor of Teaching' -- so a current bare 'Lecturer' title at any UC campus refers only to the non-Senate, definitionally non-tenure-track title, never the renamed continuing-teaching-professor series.

BYU's own Rank and Status Policy (policy.byu.edu), Section 1.1, quoted directly: 'Continuing faculty status (CFS) is a status that may be granted to members of the university's faculty, which provides for an automatic renewal of the faculty member's annual appointment,' and 'CFS is comparable to tenured status at other colleges and universities, in that it is designed to ensure the quality and consistency of the permanent faculty and to protect individual and institutional rights of academic freedom.' Section 5.2 confirms the pre-CFS/probationary period functions as BYU's tenure-track equivalent ('A faculty member's years of service prior to being granted CFS are probationary' / 'CFS-track position'). BYU's own live postings and its Workday/Chronicle listing infrastructure corroborate this directly, appending '(tenure equivalent)' to both attained ('Professorial CFS faculty (tenure equivalent)') and probationary ('Professorial CFS track (tenure equivalent)') forms. Matches bare 'CFS' so it covers both the attained-status and track/probationary forms seen in live postings ('CFS Professorial Faculty', 'CFS track Professorial Faculty', 'FT Faculty CFS Professional'). Scoped to 'Brigham Young University' (the Provo campus) only -- BYU-Hawaii and BYU-Idaho maintain separate handbooks and are not covered by this policy, so this rule is deliberately not extended to those two colleges without independently verifying their own policy language.

Notre Dame's Academic Articles, Article IV Section 1(a), define two distinct faculty categories by rank: 'Tenured and tenure-track faculty ... have the ranks of Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor, and Instructor' (Sec. 1(a)(1)) versus 'Teaching faculty are engaged primarily in teaching activities and academic program support. Teaching faculty ... have the ranks of Teaching Professor, Associate Teaching Professor, and Assistant Teaching Professor' (Sec. 1(a)(3)) -- a rank list that structurally excludes the Teaching Professor series from the tenure-eligible category by definition. Article IV Section 6 confirms directly: 'Tenure may be granted only to members of the tenured and tenure-track faculty.' Section 3(c) further documents Teaching Faculty appointments as renewable fixed terms (one year at Assistant, three years at Associate, five years at the Teaching Professor rank, with six months' notice required for non-renewal) -- the classic non-tenure-track structure, not an indefinite tenured appointment. Matches all three ranks in the Teaching Professor series as seen in live postings ('Assistant or Associate Teaching Professor - Legal Writing', 'Real Estate Teaching Professor Position'). Deliberately does not match Notre Dame's separately-governed 'Professor of the Practice' or 'Research Professor' titles (Article IV Sec. 1(a)(4)/(5), not independently verified here), nor plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Professor' with no Teaching qualifier, which remains the tenure-eligible rank.

UAB's Faculty Handbook and Policies (August 2025) establishes this through three linked provisions. Table 2.5b ('Miscellaneous Definitions for Faculty Appointments'), quoted directly: 'Credentialed Course Instructor -- Term sometimes used for contingent faculty with rank of Instructor.' Section 2.5, quoted directly: 'Contingent faculty appointments ... are non-tenure-earning.' Section 2.6.1 ('Instructor'), quoted directly, independently confirms the same conclusion by a second route: 'Appointment as Instructor is non-tenure-earning and usually requires training beyond the baccalaureate degree.' UAB's own Faculty Hiring FAQ corroborates in practice, grouping Credentialed Course Instructor hiring under the same checklist as Adjunct Faculty. Matches both real posting formats seen in live data ('...Credentialed Course Instructor-World Languages & Literatures', '...Credentialed Course Instructor-African American Studies').

University of Minnesota's own HR policy on 'Temporary or Casual Appointments', quoted directly: 'Temporary or Casual non-academic appointments ... (2) characterized by schedules that are variable, intermittent, on-call, and consistently 14 hours a week or less (casual).' The Board of Regents Policy on Faculty Tenure (Sec. 3.1), quoted directly: 'The faculty ranks are professor, associate professor, assistant professor, and instructor... Appointments at these ranks are either regular tenured or tenure-track appointments or term appointments' -- 'Casual' is not among the ranks this policy governs at all, confirming it is a non-academic HR classification entirely outside the tenure structure (matches live posting 'AI/ML Instructor - Casual'). Separately, UMN's Administrative Policy 'Academic Appointments with Teaching Functions' documents Academic Professional and Administrative (P&A) titles including 'Teaching Specialist' and 'Assistant Extension Professor' as non-faculty appointment categories; the companion P&A appointment-types policy states directly: 'Regulations governing academic tenure do not apply in these cases.' Deliberately does not match plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Associate Professor'/'Instructor' with no Casual/Teaching Specialist/Extension qualifier, nor UMN's 'Academic/Clinician Track' compound postings (genuinely spanning two possible outcomes) -- both correctly stay unclassified.

rules.college: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
rules.note: Rutgers Biomedical and Health Sciences' governing 'Policies and Guidelines... of the Faculty' (A&P Guidelines, Oct. 2020), Section I.B, quoted directly: 'These goals will be achieved by faculty appointed to one of five different tracks: a tenure track, and four non-tenure tracks' -- Teaching Track, Clinical Track (with Clinical Scholar and Clinical Educator sub-types), Professional Practice Track, and Research Track. 'Tenure may be granted only to faculty on the Tenure Track,' and non-tenure-track titles are explicitly documented as carrying an appended track suffix (e.g. 'Assistant Professor, Clinical Track'), distinct from the unsuffixed Tenure Track title ('Assistant Professor (Tenure Track only)'). Corroborated by NJMS's own Provost Q&A for faculty: 'ONLY ON TENURE TRACK. THERE IS NO UP OR OUT ON THE FOUR NON-TENURE TRACKS,' using 'Clinical Educator Track' verbatim. Matches the track-suffix convention seen in live postings ('Assistant Professor, Clinical Educator Track'). IMPORTANT: per this same source, a plain, unmodified 'Assistant Professor'/'Associate Professor'/'Professor' at Rutgers RBHS is presumptively Tenure Track by Rutgers' own naming convention (the Tenure Track title carries no suffix) -- unlike many peer academic medical centers, this rule intentionally does NOT extend to bare rank titles or a 'Clinical [rank]' prefix convention, since no evidence supports that pattern at Rutgers.

rules.college: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
rules.note: Direct extension of the companion rule above, encoding the conclusion its own note already reached but left uncoded ('a plain, unmodified Assistant/Associate/Professor at Rutgers RBHS is presumptively Tenure Track'). The A&P Guidelines' own title tables are a complete enumeration, not an example: the Tenure Track table lists only 'Assistant Professor (Tenure Track only) / Associate Professor / Professor / Distinguished Professor' with no suffix, while EACH of the four non-tenure tracks' tables append an explicit track-name suffix to the identical rank words ('Assistant Professor, Teaching Track', '..., Clinical Track', '..., Professional Practice Track', '..., Research Track') -- so a title containing 'Professor' with none of those four suffixes, and no bare 'Clinical Scholar'/'Clinical Educator' sub-type label (the Clinical Track's own two named sub-types, which can appear without the word 'Track' attached, e.g. a live posting titled 'Lymphoma Clinical Scholar, Faculty Physician'), is Tenure Track by elimination rather than by absence-of-evidence. Scoped as a companion to the existing rule (checked first; this one only fires when that one's track-suffix pattern does not match). Applied at the 'Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey' college level since the dataset does not separately distinguish RBHS from Rutgers' other units, but every live posting this rule currently resolves is itself a health-sciences department (Ob/Gyn, Neurology, Psychiatry, Oncology, Cardiology, Nursing, Surgery), consistent with the cited source's own RBHS scope.

Troy's own applicant-tracking system (troyuniversityjobs.com, Troy-owned, not a third party) carries a structured 'Tenure Track Status' field on every posting. Multiple current bare-'Lecturer' postings confirm 'Non-Tenure Track' directly (e.g. posting F1077P, Lecturer, Sorrell College of Business: 'a full-time, non-tenure track faculty appointment on a ten-month contract'; posting F1086P, Lecturer of Nursing: Tenure Track Status 'Non-Tenure Track'). The Faculty Handbook itself (cited at troy.edu/epolicy/300-academics.html, Sec. 3.2.2.2, as classifying Lecturer under 'Unranked Faculty') is gated behind Troy's SSO login and could not be independently read, so this rule rests on Troy's own live hiring-system data rather than the Handbook text. By contrast, Troy's own system explicitly labels compound 'Lecturer/Assistant/Associate Professor' postings as 'Dependent on selected rank' -- confirmed genuinely ambiguous by real examples resolving to either outcome (posting F1072P, 'Lecturer/Assistant Professor', resolved Tenure Track; posting F0893P, same compound pattern, resolved differently) -- so titlePattern deliberately excludes any 'Lecturer/...' compound and matches only a standalone 'Lecturer' title.

rules.college: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center-New Orleans
rules.note: LSUHSC-NO's own Faculty Handbook (Rev. April 2025), Section 2.1.1, lists 'Research - Instructor / Assistant Professor / Associate Professor / Professor' as a rank series structurally separate from the plain 'Assistant Professor / Associate Professor / Professor' tenure-track series, and ties rank definitions to LSU System Permanent Memorandum 23 (PM-23, last revised July 2, 2025). PM-23 Section I.P, quoted directly: 'Only individuals whose primary responsibility is conducting research or extension education and who often are paid from grant or contract funds are to be appointed to these ranks,' and 'Individuals in these ranks do not acquire tenure through the passage of time and may become tenured only by specific individual recommendation through appropriate channels and approval by the President.' Note this is a weaker signal than PM-23's Clinical series (Section R) or Professional Practice series (Section T), each of which states outright 'This is non-tenure track' -- the Research series instead functions as non-tenure-accruing by policy design (no automatic tenure clock) rather than being categorically barred from tenure, so this rule is scoped narrowly to the '[Rank] - Research' suffix form seen in live postings (e.g. 'Assistant Professor - Research') rather than to any broader inference. Deliberately does not match the bare 'Assistant Professor/ Associate Professor/ Professor' enumeration with no Research qualifier, which PM-23 Section E confirms tenures automatically after 7 years by default and correctly stays unclassified.

rules.college: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center-New Orleans
rules.note: Direct extension of the companion Research-series rule above, using the stronger evidence its own note already flagged but did not yet encode. LSU System Permanent Memorandum 23 (PM-23, rev. July 2, 2025) Section I.R ('Assistant Professor of Clinical ____ / Associate Professor of Clinical ____ / Professor of Clinical ____', for any clinical specialty), quoted directly: '1. Criteria -- This is non-tenure track for full-time faculty in the clinical sciences...' and '3. Tenure and Appointment -- Tenure is not awarded to individuals holding these ranks.' Section II.E (the parallel part-time/prefix form 'Clinical Instructor / Clinical Assistant Professor / Clinical Associate Professor / Clinical Professor'), quoted directly: '3. Tenure and Appointment -- Personnel holding one of these ranks do not receive tenure.' Section I.T ('Assistant Professor- Professional Practice / Associate Professor- Professional Practice / Professor- Professional Practice'), quoted directly: '1. Criteria -- This is a non-tenure track for full-time faculty in the professions...' and '3. Tenure and Appointment -- Tenure is not awarded to individuals holding these ranks.' Live LSUHSC-NO postings render the Clinical designation with a comma or dash rather than PM-23's own 'of Clinical' wording (e.g. 'Assistant Professor / Associate Professor / Professor, Clinical - Pediatric Cardiologist', 'Professor - Clinical, Psychiatry'), so titlePattern matches all three observed forms (prefix 'Clinical [rank]', suffix 'of Clinical', and ', Clinical'/'- Clinical'). Does NOT extend to the live postings' 'Instruction Track' qualifier (e.g. 'Instruction Track Chsp/Epph') -- that phrase appears nowhere in either PM-23 or the LSUHSC-NO Faculty Handbook, so it stays unclassified rather than being guessed.

The University of Toledo College of Medicine and Life Sciences' own 'Faculty Tracks for Academic Rank and Criteria for Promotion and Tenure' (March 2023), quoted directly (p.2, 'Designation of Title'): 'All full-time faculty members, except for Community-based faculty and Adjunct faculty, will have the same title... Community-based faculty members will have their title preceded by "Clinical", for example, "Clinical Professor of Surgery".' The Community-Based Track is explicitly labeled non-tenure ('Non-Tenure Track', p.35) with ranks Clinical Assistant/Associate/Professor. Separately, UToledo's main-campus Lecturers collective bargaining agreement, quoted directly (Sec. 8.1.1): 'Lecturers are full-time Non-tenure-track faculty Members,' with its Recognition clause (Art. 2.1) explicitly excluding 'all Tenured and Tenure-track faculty.' IMPORTANT scope note: per the same COMLS policy, a plain, unmodified rank title (e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Surgery') is used identically across FOUR tenure-eligible tracks (Academic Basic Scientist, Basic Science Educator, Clinical Scholar, Clinical Educator) and TWO non-tenure tracks (Research Track, Practitioner Track) -- the plain title is genuinely non-diagnostic by the institution's own design, so titlePattern deliberately does not match it, only the 'Clinical [rank]' and 'Lecturer' forms that ARE reliable per-track signals.

Georgia Tech's Faculty Handbook (Policy Library 3.2, 'Non-Tenure Track Faculty'), quoted directly: 'Individuals employed in non-tenure track positions shall not be eligible for consideration for the award of tenure.' Section 3.2.2 enumerates the non-tenure-track Academic Faculty title series -- 'Professor of the Practice' ('a non-tenurable title'), 'Academic Professional' (incl. Associate/Senior/Principal, 'not a tenure-track position') -- and the Provost's official 'List of Faculty Titles' additionally lists the Research Faculty series (Research Associate/Engineer/Scientist/Technologist, Extension Professional) as a membership category distinct from Academic Faculty's tenure-eligible professorial ranks. Section 3.3.1 confirms 'only Academic Faculty members in the professorial ranks can be in the Tenure Track' -- i.e. only the unmodified 'Professor (Assistant, Associate, Full, Regents)' line. Confirmed against live GT postings using this exact split (e.g. 'Open Rank, Non-Tenure Track Academic Professional or Sr. Academic Professional' at School of Physics vs. explicitly-labeled '(tenure-track)' Assistant/Associate Professor postings elsewhere).

rules.titlePattern: \b(?:Instructor|Assistant Professor|Associate Professor|Professor),\s*Research\b|\bResearch\s+(?:Instructor|Assistant Professor|Associate Professor|Professor)\b|\bProfessor of Instruction\b|\bProfessor of Practice\b|\b(?:Professorial\s+)?Lecturer\b|\b(?:Adjunct\s+|Senior\s+)?Clinical Supervisor\b|\b(?:Senior\s+)?Instructor Librarian\b
rules.note: USA's Faculty Handbook (Sept. 2025 edition) documents several distinct non-tenure title series, each quoted directly: 'Instructor, Research'/'Assistant Professor, Research'/etc. -- 'a faculty appointment, but is not tenure-accruing' (Sec. 3.20.9, 3.20.1.3); the main-campus instructional series 'Assistant Professor of Instruction / Associate Professor of Instruction / Professor of Instruction' (Sec. 3.15.5, listed under 'Non-tenure track instructional faculty'); 'Professor of Practice' ('The non-tenure track faculty position, Professor of Practice...', Sec. 3.2.5); 'Professorial Lecturer'/'Lecturer' ('Service in either capacity does not qualify a person for tenure', Sec. 3.2.6); 'Clinical Supervisor' (College of Education and Professional Studies, 'Clinical appointments are non-tenure track', Sec. 3.5.1); and 'Instructor Librarian'/'Senior Instructor Librarian' ('non-tenure only'). IMPORTANT: at the Whiddon College of Medicine and USA Health, a plain, unmodified rank title (e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Surgery') is shared identically across BOTH the tenure-accruing Investigator/Educator tracks and the non-tenure Clinician track (Sec. 3.20.1.2: 'Appointments to the Investigator and Educator tracks can be tenure-accruing or on a non-tenure basis'), so titlePattern deliberately does not match bare rank titles -- only the specifically-named non-tenure series above. One known edge case not specially handled: a posting offering both a bare rank AND a qualified series as alternatives in the same title (e.g. 'Assistant Professor or Assistant Professor of Instruction') will still match on the qualified alternative even though the bare alternative is genuinely undetermined -- a narrow, low-frequency imprecision accepted here rather than engineering a fix for one posting.

Clemson's Faculty Manual (Ch. IV, Sec. C.2, 'Other Faculty Designations'), quoted directly: 'No faculty appointments in other designations are tenurable, although appointments may be renewed.' This section enumerates: Research Faculty (research professor/research associate professor/research assistant professor), Extension Faculty (extension professor/etc.), Clinical Faculty (clinical professor/etc.), Lecturer/Senior Lecturer/Principal Lecturer, Professor of Practice, and Post-Doctoral Research Fellow. By contrast, Ch. IV Sec. C.1 'Tenured and Tenure Track Faculty' uses unmodified Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor (plus Instructor and corresponding Library ranks -- Instructor is deliberately excluded from this rule since the Manual itself calls it 'not a tenurable rank' while grouping it under the tenure-track designation, a genuine ambiguity left unresolved). Confirmed against live HigherEdJobs postings: 'Senior Lecturer' listings are explicitly self-labeled non-tenure-track while plain 'Assistant Professor' listings are explicitly self-labeled tenure-track.

MSU's Bylaws for Academic Governance, Sec. 1.1.1, quoted directly: '1.1.1.1. The regular faculty shall consist of all persons appointed under the rules of tenure and holding the rank of professor, associate professor, or assistant professor... 1.1.1.2. The fixed-term faculty shall consist of all persons holding the rank of professor, associate professor, assistant professor, or instructor, but not appointed under the rules of tenure. 1.1.1.5. The Academic Specialists shall consist of persons holding the rank of senior specialist, specialist with continuing appointment, specialist with probationary appointment, or fixed-term specialist' -- a wholly separate appointment system governed by its own continuing-appointment framework, not the tenure system (corroborated by the Academic Specialist Manual Sec. 1.2). The Instructor/Senior Instructor rank is never part of the tenure-eligible 'regular faculty' rank list (limited to professor/associate professor/assistant professor) -- MSU's own Fixed-Term Faculty policy page confirms 'Fixed-term faculty members are ranked faculty (instructor, senior instructor, assistant/associate/full professor) who are appointed outside of the tenure system.' IMPORTANT: MSU explicitly uses the SAME professor/associate professor/assistant professor titles for both regular (tenure) and fixed-term (non-tenure) faculty (1.1.1.1 vs 1.1.1.2), so titlePattern deliberately does not match bare Professor ranks -- only Academic Specialist and Instructor/Senior Instructor, which are unambiguous outside the tenure system by rank alone.

Augusta University's Faculty Classification Policy (Policy No. 438), quoted directly: 'Faculty are classified as tenured, non-tenured on track, not in a tenure type position, or other.' The policy's own classification table lists 'Research faculty ... Assistant Research Scientist, Research Scientist, Senior Research Scientist, or Principal Research Scientist' with tenure status 'Other'; 'Non-Tenure Track' ranks including Lecturer and Senior Lecturer; and 'Other -- Clinical Faculty' ranks (Clinical Instructor, Assistant/Associate Clinical Professor, Clinical Professor), described as non-paid faculty 'not considered to be members of the faculty or Corps of Instruction.' IMPORTANT: AU's own policy states the core ranks 'Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor' appear identically in BOTH the Tenure Track and Non-Tenure Track classification lists ('Non-tenure-track faculty can be classified as lecturer, senior lecturer, instructor, assistant professor, associate professor, or professor') -- so titlePattern deliberately does not match bare rank titles or 'Open Rank' postings (no analogous named policy exists for 'Open Rank' at AU, unlike Ohio State's documented precedent, but the underlying title-ambiguity conclusion is the same), only the Research Scientist, Lecturer, and Clinical [rank] series that ARE reliable non-tenure signals.

rules.titlePattern: ^(?:(?:Senior\s+)?Academic Professional(?:\s+Associate)?|(?:Senior\s+|Principal\s+)?Lecturer|Public Service (?:Representative|Assistant|Associate)|Senior Public Service Associate|Clinical (?:Instructor|Assistant Professor|Associate Professor|Professor)|(?:Assistant|Associate|Senior) Research Scientist|Librarian (?:I|II|III|IV)|Staff Physician)\b
rules.note: UGA's Office of Faculty Affairs (Provost's Office) publishes its full faculty rank taxonomy at provost.uga.edu, listing 'Academic' (Instructor/Assistant/Associate/Professor -- the tenure-ladder category) as one of ten categories alongside nine others: Academic Professional, Clinical, Lecturer, Librarian, Public Service, Research Scientists, Administrative A, and Staff Physician. UGA's own Non-Tenure-Track Faculty Learning Community site (nontenuretrack.uga.edu), quoted directly: 'UGA's faculty ranks include not only the academic rank tenured/tenure-track faculty (professors, associate professors, and assistant professors) but also nine other types of faculty,' and lists 'Academic Professionals, Clinical faculty, Lecturer, Librarian, Public Service, Research Scientist, Instructor, Administrative A, Staff Physician' as UGA's 'non-tenure-eligible faculty roles.' IMPORTANT: UGA's own two source pages contradict each other on bare 'Instructor' (one page groups it with the tenure ladder, the other lists it as one of the nine non-tenure-eligible types), so titlePattern deliberately excludes bare Instructor -- only the unambiguous series (Academic Professional, Clinical [rank], Lecturer, Librarian I-IV, Public Service [titles], Research Scientist, Staff Physician) are matched. Confirmed against live UGA postings using this exact convention (e.g. 'Academic Professional Track (Non-Tenure): Associate Professor of the Practice...', 'Lecturer (non-tenure track)', 'Public Service Associate').

CAU's Faculty Handbook (approved by the Board of Trustees May 17, 2013), Sec. 1.2.1.2-1.2.1.4, describes Lecturer/Senior Lecturer/Master Lecturer purely as annual, capped-term reappointments with no tenure language, and Sec. 1.9.3 ('Eligibility for Third-Year Review') confirms this directly: 'The purpose of the "Third-Year Review" is to assist tenure-track faculty to assess their progress toward tenure... Continuing lecturers are also subject to Third-Year Reviews to assess their progress toward promotion' -- explicitly treating 'tenure-track faculty' and 'continuing lecturers' as two distinct categories. Sec. 1.2.2.5, quoted directly: 'Scholars-in-Residence are non-tenure-track, non-tenured faculty.' Sec. 1.2.3, quoted directly: Research Scientists (and sub-ranks Senior Scholars/Principal Research Scientists, Senior Research Associates/Scientists, Research Associates/Scientists, Research Assistants) '...are not notice/tenure-track appointments, and therefore are not eligible for tenure.' IMPORTANT: bare 'Instructor' is genuinely ambiguous per this same handbook (Sec. 1.2.1.5 describes it as a capped feeder rank, but Sec. 1.9.2 counts Instructor-rank service toward the tenure probationary clock) -- deliberately excluded from titlePattern.

Wayne State's Board of Governors Code, Statute 2.51.01.030, quoted directly (independently verified against the live bog.wayne.edu page): 'Effective August 1, 1983, appointments to the positions only of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, and Professor are tenure-track appointments.' University Policy 03-2 ('Position Descriptions and Terms of Appointment for Non-Tenure-Track Faculty...', independently verified against the live policies.wayne.edu page) defines three parallel non-tenure classifications using the SAME rank names with a parenthetical qualifier: 'Faculty (teaching) titles include instructor (teaching), assistant professor (teaching)...' ('a full or fractional-time non-tenure track classification'), and likewise for '(research)' and '(clinical)' -- the latter 'limited to wholly clinical faculty positions in clinical departments of the School of Medicine, College of Nursing, [and] Eugene Applebaum College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences.' Section 11 additionally defines 'Faculty Full-time Affiliate (FTA)' titles using a ' FTA' suffix on the same rank names (with or without the parenthetical), also non-tenure-track per the policy's own title and scope. IMPORTANT: a SEPARATE 'Instructor' classification (Sec. 3.1, capped at 2 years, used when a doctorate is incomplete) is also non-tenure but uses the bare word 'Instructor' with no qualifier -- genuinely indistinguishable in title text from the tenure-track Instructor rank per BOG 2.51.01.030, so titlePattern deliberately requires the '(teaching/research/clinical)' or ' FTA' marker and never matches a bare rank title.

Rice University Policy 201 ('Faculty Appointments, Promotions and Tenure'), Section 1, quoted directly: tenure-track ranks are only 'Assistant professor, Associate professor, and (Full) professor.' Non-tenure-track promotable ranks are separately, explicitly named: 'Assistant research professor, Associate research professor, and (Full) research professor,' 'Assistant teaching professor, Associate teaching professor, and (Full) teaching professor,' and 'Lecturer, and Senior lecturer' -- each defined as non-tenure-eligible ('By definition, non-tenure-track faculty ranks do not carry tenure and are not tenure eligible'). Section 1.b.2 ('Other non-tenure-track faculty ranks') additionally and unambiguously lists 'Professor in the practice rank' and 'Instructor rank' with no contradicting language elsewhere in the policy -- unlike some peer institutions, Rice's own source contains no ambiguity about Instructor, so it is included here. 'Professor in the Practice' uses Rice's own distinct phrasing ('Professor in the Practice of [Field]'), separate from the generic 'professor of practice' already caught globally. Confirmed against live Rice postings using this exact convention (e.g. 'Lecturer/Assistant Teaching Professor of Health Sciences').

NC State's REG 05.20.34 defines Lecturer as part of 'Professional faculty,' explicitly 'not eligible for consideration or conferral of permanent tenure.' Live postings sometimes offer Lecturer alongside a 'Teaching Assistant Professor' alternative (e.g. 'Lecturer or Teaching Assistant Professor in Political Science') -- both are NC State's non-tenure-track professional-faculty titles, so this does not introduce the kind of tenure/non-tenure ambiguity seen at other institutions' compound titles.

University of Miami's Faculty Manual states directly: 'Lecturers do not hold tenured or tenure-earning appointments.' Live postings occasionally offer 'Lecturer or Senior Lecturer' as alternatives -- both are non-tenure Lecturer-series ranks, so no ambiguity is introduced.

rules.college: Columbia University in the City of New York
rules.note: 'Lecturer in Discipline' and 'Senior Lecturer in Discipline' are Columbia's own formally defined, renewable non-ladder teaching titles, distinct from the tenure-track Assistant/Associate/Professor ladder. Deliberately scoped to this exact phrase rather than bare 'Lecturer': Columbia postings also use plain 'Lecturer in [Hebrew/Korean/Sanskrit and Tamil/etc.]' language-instruction titles that were not independently verified against this same non-tenure convention, and titles combining Lecturer with Instructor/Assistant Professor/Visiting Professor as genuine multi-track alternatives (e.g. 'Lecturer, Instructor, or Assistant Professor') are correctly excluded and stay unclassified rather than guessed.
Kennesaw State's Faculty Handbook contains a section explicitly titled 'Non-Tenure Track Lecturer Faculty Ranks,' confirming Lecturer (all levels) is outside the tenure system.

University of North Texas Policy 06.005 ('Non-Tenure Track Faculty Reappointment and Promotion') governs UNT's Lecturer/Professional Faculty titles as a category structurally separate from the tenure system. Scoped to the Denton main campus only ('University of North Texas'); not extended to University of North Texas at Dallas or the Health Science Center, which were not independently verified.

University of Hawaii Executive Policy E5.221 defines 'Lecturer' as 'persons employed for short-term teaching assignments, usually on a part-time basis' -- a category structurally separate from the tenure-eligible Instructor/Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor (I3-I5) ranks. This is a UH System-wide executive policy. Scoped to the exact college string 'University of Hawaii System' as it appears in the live dataset (an umbrella entry under which the live Lecturer/Lecturer-CC postings are actually filed, rather than a specific campus).

rules.collegePattern: ^(?:CUNY Bernard M Baruch College|CUNY Borough of Manhattan Community College|CUNY Bronx Community College|CUNY Brooklyn College|CUNY City College|CUNY Graduate School and University Center|CUNY Hunter College|CUNY John Jay College of Criminal Justice|CUNY LaGuardia Community College|CUNY New York City College of Technology|CUNY Queens College|CUNY Queensborough Community College|CUNY School of Law|CUNY School of Professional Studies|CUNY Stella and Charles Guttman Community College|CUNY York College|College of Staten Island CUNY)$
rules.note: UNUSUAL CASE -- this is the one confirmed exception to the otherwise-near-universal US convention that bare 'Lecturer' is non-tenure-track (verified this session against ~15 other institutions with zero other exceptions found). The PSC-CUNY collective bargaining agreement (the governing document for faculty titles across every CUNY senior and community college under one master contract), Article 11.1, quoted directly: 'The title Lecturer shall be a tenure-bearing (certificate of continuous employment) title used for full-time members of the faculty who are hired to teach and perform related faculty functions, but do not have a research commitment.' Article 12 confirms the mechanism: a full-time Lecturer becomes eligible for a Certificate of Continuous Employment (CCE) after five years, which 'carries with it the guarantee of full-time reappointment' terminable only for cause -- functionally the same permanent-employment protection tenure provides, even though CUNY's own formal terminology names the status 'CCE' rather than 'tenure.' Given the contract's own classification article calls the title itself 'tenure-bearing,' this is treated as tenure-track=true. 'Adjunct Lecturer' postings are unaffected -- already resolved to non-tenure by the global 'adjunct' keyword shortcut before this institution rule is ever reached. Excludes the prefix form 'Doctoral Lecturer' (as opposed to the suffix/parenthetical '(Doctoral Schedule)' form, which reads as a compensation-schedule detail for lecturers holding a doctorate, not a different appointment category) out of genuine uncertainty over whether it denotes the same full-time tenure-bearing title -- a small number of postings left conservatively unclassified rather than guessed. Excludes CUNY System Office, CUNY Start, and CUNY Language (non-degree-granting program/administrative entities, not independently confirmed to be covered by the same faculty title schedule).
